utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Jadranko Prlic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, registrar. Today we are Thursday, the 17th of January, 2008. I would like to greet all the representatives of the Prosecution, Defence counsel, the accused, as well as all the people assisting us. Now, we shall begin by finishing the cross-examination of the witness. When the witness leaves, the Trial Chamber will hand down oral decisions, important oral decisions, after having heard the Prosecutor prior to that on one of its oral decisions, but we will do this after the witness has finished testifying. The -- we shall resume the cross-examination. It's Mr. Praljak's Defence counsel who is going to resume, after which Ms. Alaburic will take the floor. I'd like to give the registrar for four IC numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, four lists of documents have been tendered through Witness Cedric Thornberry. Prosecution list will become Exhibit IC 780. Stojic Defence list will become Exhibit IC 781. Praljak Defence list will become Exhibit IC 782. And Petkovic Defence exhibit -- list will become Exhibit IC 783.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You may sit down. I shall give the floor to General Praljak's counsel, who has a number of questions to put to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Good afternoon to everyone in the courtroom, especially to Their Honours, and everybody in and around the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Witness. We speak the same language, you and I, so you don't have to wait for an interpretation. You understand me straight away. But please make short breaks between my question and your answer to facilitate the work of the interpreters so that everybody in the courtroom can follow us. So we'll try and speak slowly and make pauses in between.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, could the usher provide the witness with a folder that we provided yesterday, and could the usher while he's there, while he's on his feet -- well, there's one document there in that folder. For the record it is document P 08461. It is a document signed by Mesinja [phoen] Mahmutovic from your own town. It was compiled on the 22nd of February, 1994. Have you opened the document? For the record, the document was used yesterday by the Prosecutor. [In English] I would kindly ask usher to assist the witness. Obviously there is some problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now you have the document, which you saw yesterday; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I'd just like to ask you the following with respect to that document: The person under number 15, it says Likic Medina, Sulejman, father's name, also was killed, and yesterday you said she was a fighter. Now, other people need not understand this, but judging by the name, that's a female. It's a woman, is it not?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Now, in the days before the conflict, did she wear a camouflage jacket?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She wore a camouflage jacket because she was a cook in the kitchen cooking for the army in Stupni Do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right. And her status was the status of fighter; right?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Combatant?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Now, let's clear something else up linked to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Does the witness have the Prosecution folder in front of him? If not, could the usher help us out here, please. [In English] In Prosecution folder the document number P 08659. 8659. It should be there. Okay. Then if it isn't, I would kindly ask you to take mine and put it on ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, have you seen the document?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Is from the records of dead, death certificate. Now, is that the same person that we saw in the list in the previous document under number 15?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, I will not need any more this document. Thank you. I'd like to show a video now Your Honours, the transcript of which is under 3D 01138, and the video itself has the following number: P 05522. We received the video from the Prosecution, and as we had a break between yesterday and today, we were able to take this out of the documentation. And the Prosecution devoted quite a lot of time showing the photographs of the trenches around Stupni Do, so I think the best thing would be to see a video of those trenches so that we can gain a complete picture. May we have the video shown, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] The village of Stupni Do itself was long prepared for the execution of this criminal plan. How else could one explain the existence of a significant number of well fortified trenches wherefrom one has a grandstand view of Vares. "These bunkers along with the Bogos elevation encircle the village of Stupni Do which from this vantage point does not look as harmless as one wants to show, unfortunately, even in many world newspapers. "The distribution of bunkers and trenches was such that the Croatian locations under the elevation, as well as the village itself, could be under undisturbed fire. "Here is one of the houses which was a bunker itself. The facade says it all. "Close to the house was one of the best fortified trenches which gives a view of Majdan Vares. "From the other side of the same elevation is the Croatian village of Mir. And right next to it is the Catholic cemetery. "And that's a Croatian house there that was destroyed in the heavy fighting."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Counsel. Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The video continues, but there is no more footage showing the trenches around Stupni Do and Bogos, so I don't think we need play it any further. We received the video from the Prosecution, I repeat, and as far as I can see from the material attached, we can see that they received it previously from the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Now, Witness, I have one question for you. You've seen this video. Do you happen to have seen that footage on television some time before?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I've never seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Well, yesterday there was quite a lot of discussion during your testimony about that, and you were shown photographs, and on the photographs you indicated the trenches that you were able to see. Now that you've seen the video, are those the same trenches that we talked about yesterday?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't recognise anything there, to be quite frank. I didn't recognise anything. The trench that you could see, Vares Majdan, well, there's one at Bogos -- well, I don't know. You can't see it from this vantage point, from Vares Majdan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, not to waste time, there were a number of photographs from Bogos and the other side down towards the village. Did you recognise the village as being your own village?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to be quite frank, I didn't recognise it as being my village. It's not quite clear to me. I didn't recognise the houses. I looked at the photograph, but the only thing that I could recognise was the house next to the cemetery, Mahmutovic Dervis, and the former shop where Mir and Stupni Do were supplied with goods.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So can I put it this way: You say you didn't recognise it. So it's a matter of human perception. Do you state that they are not photographs of Stupni Do and the surrounding parts and the trenches around Stupni Do, including Bogos hill? Can you say no, that is not it, or is what you're saying, "I just can't recognise it"? There's a difference there, you know.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be quite frank, I can't recognise any of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Except for the two features that you told us of a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So you recognise those facilities and features as belonging to your village?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I don't think there's any point in showing the video again, Your Honours. I think what we've shown is sufficient. I can't speak of authenticity but I do believe in its authenticity because as I say the material was provided to us by the Prosecution and the Prosecution got it from the BH government, so it's certainly authentic. And from our own knowledge and information, members of our team were in Stupni Do, they toured the area and were quite certain that that is what it depicts. I would like to thank the witness. I have no further questions, but I would like to table a request now to the Trial Chamber in keeping with their previous decision of the 10th of May last year to allow General Praljak to ask several questions. My arguments in favour of that are the same as for Witness Mahmutovic of the 12th of December last year. If need be I can repeat that, but I don't want to waste time unless you specifically ask me to go and explain again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before General Praljak puts questions, I have a question to put to you which is in line with this video, we can, if need be, all watch again. This video shows that there is, at the least, one trenches -- one trench that overlooks Vares Majdan, and just alongside it there is a house. This house, according to the video, was also a bunker. On watching the video, I say to myself that when you are standing in this trench Vares Majdan is two or three kilometres away as the crow flies, and therefore where this trench is positioned one has a strategic overview. So are you challenging that there is a trench there, or are you not challenging it? If you like, we can watch the video again. It's a very short one. I think the best would be to display it again, please. Can we display the video again, please. So we shall look at it again. So have a close look at this. [Videotape played].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] The village of Stupni Do itself was long prepared for the execution of this criminal plan. How else could one explain the existence of significant number of well-fortified trenches where from one has a grandstand view of Vares. "These bunkers along with Bogos elevation encircled the village of Stupni Do, which from this point of view does not look as harmless as one wants to show, unfortunately, even in many international newspapers. "The arrangement of bunkers and trenches was such that the Croatian locations under the elevation, as well as the village itself, could be under constant fire. "This is one of the houses that was itself a bunker. This facade says it all. "Close to the house there is one of the best fortified trenches which commands a view of Majdan Vares. "On the other side of the same elevation there is a Croatian village Mir, and next to it the Catholic graveyard."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, sir, we've just seen the video again. We've seen a trench, and from this trench we can see Vares Majdan directly, and at one stage the camera is zooming in, and you can just about see the windows of the houses. Are you challenging -- are you challenging this? What do you have to say to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were no houses close to our trenches. The trench that I just saw from which you could see Vares Majdan, that was the trench on the top of Borova Glava. Partly it faced Vares Majdan, and partly it faced the Nisic plateau. As for the other trenches, I'm not familiar with any of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So you've identified a trench that overlooks Vares Majdan. So you can confirm that there was a trench there, but on the other hand you say you do not recognise the other trenches.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I'm saying is that there was a trench at Borova Glava locality which I have just recognise, and you could see Vares Majdan from there. But the closest house is more than 200 metres away. The houses that I saw in the footage was the house of Halid Likic, and there was no trench there ever. There was just the house which still stands there today, and it hasn't been refurbished. Next to it is a pathway or a road, and there are no trenches anywhere near that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The trench at Borova Glava, when the village was attacked were there ABiH soldiers in this trench?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Were they killed? Were they detained? Did they run away? What happened with the men in this trench?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, and as far as from what I heard, I did not see anything myself because I wasn't there, nobody was killed in that trench. They just had to abandon the trenches. They had to flee. I don't know what -- how else to put that. We're talking about this trench on Borova Glava.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. General Praljak -- yes, Mr. Flynn.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Just one matter, Mr. President if I may ask Mr. Kovacic just on a point of information. The transcript -- Mr. Kovacic. I'm sorry. The transcript that accompanied the video might be regarded as somewhat Partisan from the Croat standpoint of view. May I ask was this transcript -- is this an assessment of the Defence, the transcript that accompanied the video, or is this a transcript that accompanied the original video coming from the BiH? I have never seen the video before and that's why I ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kovacic, in the documents you gave us a translation in English of what seems to accompany the -- the video. So the translation, is this the translation of the comments by the journalist that can be heard on the video, or does it come from somewhere else? Please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in the folder that you have just mentioned, there are two documents. One is a surrogate [indiscernible] videos, and that is a Prosecutor's document that accompanies the video. This is document that we received together with the video, and that is in e-court. It arises from that document where the video comes from, and I base my assumption that the Prosecutor provided us with a video on that document and the Prosecution received it from the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The other document, 3D 018, and with the words "Office translation" in the right-hand corner, this is what my staff transcribed earlier this morning. They just transcribed a comment of the anchor that is heard on the video. I'm not claiming that this is a perfect translation, but what we could hear, what we could transcribe we did in good faith, and while the witness was watching the video I could hear the interpreters to -- who were trying to interpret from the video footage, and this is more or less the same what we did. And the video itself was disclosed to us by the Prosecution according to Rule 65, and that's it. And I don't know anything else about its origin. I accept bona fides that this is material that -- that originates from the Prosecution as the material that originates from the former Yugoslavia and that it is credible because they were provided with the governments of the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Flynn, you should know these documents since it is the Office of the Prosecutor who disclosed it to the Defence. And when you take a look at the second document video, there are in fact -- there are two different documents, and what we've just seen should be the second video which was shot by the Kiseljak television, and it is indicated that it was a propaganda in favour of the HVO. There should also be interviews with Croats expelled from villages around Vares. This video seems to be much longer than the clip that we've just seen since it's indicated here that there are also interviews of Croats. But the document also indicates that it is something coming from the Kiseljak television.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: I had seen that and I was just inquiring as to whether or not the -- the short summary which accompanied the video was an extract from that or was it an assessment made by the Defence themselves, but I think I'm clear on the point now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just for the record I believe that there may have been a misunderstanding here. The video contains other things, but according to my modest opinion for this witness I have used only one part of the video. There are other stories in there that are not necessarily connected, and the transcript that we provided with the document, 3D 01138. It says here that what we're showing is the part of the footage between 09.25 and 12.30. The words that you heard were transcribed by our team. This is what we wanted to show. We denoted the time on the video as the time that we want to use with this witness. The Prosecutor can use this part or any other parts, and they are more than welcome to use whatever they want to use. I've selected this part because it's relevant for the witness that we are -- we see here today. Yesterday the witness spoke about the trenches. He was provided with the photos of the trenches, and we all know from experience that the information that we receive based on photos, video differ from what can be seen on the ground, and that's what I wanted to obtain, the identification of those trenches. If my learned friend has problems with the authenticity of this material, I appreciate that, but I was not the one who provided the video to them. It was the other way around.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Just to have no doubts in the ear. The part that we have been shown is a part of the second footage that is mentioned here; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is one of the same video, but it is somewhat longer and I have only taken one excerpt, and in the description surrogate sheet you can see that there are different parts. I have concentrated just on one part that was relevant for this witness, but it's all one video footage, one long video footage from which I just took one part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: That is clear to me. What I'm referring to is that the document mentions, first in a small paragraph, first footage, and then a longer paragraph, second footage. The second footage here is accompanied by certain comments which are, as it seems, not related to the first footage, and I just wanted to make sure, and it is likely because the first footage only seems to be in the morgue, that it is an excerpt of the -- of what is here called "Second footage 05:51 to 32:20. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone for the counsel. Microphone for the counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry very much. [Interpretation] Now I understand your question. You can see from the surrogate sheet that these are two video footages. We did not touch their first one. We did not use the first one. We used the second one and only one part from the second video that you have just seen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And to be entirely clear, the transcript in your document 3D 1138 is the Croatian version of the comments made by the journalist, and the English version, that is the translation of such comments, because it starts in English with "The village of Stupni Do itself," and then it continues from there.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is our office of translation. This is not a CLSS translation. If anybody contests our office translation, I'm going to send it to CLSS for official translation, but I don't see the point. This is just a courtesy for others to be able to follow. And we heard all these words in Croatian. They have been translated by our office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. General Praljak to conclude. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, please limit yourself to technical questions, military questions, but you know this already. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] It goes without saying that I should do that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Likic.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: You will appreciate that this Court needs to investigate certain details. I appreciate your family tragedy, and I don't wish in any way or form to hurt your feelings by my questions. However, in order to clarify the whole situation, some questions need to be asked and they will be of military and technical and mathematical nature. First of all, I would like the usher to put this photo in front of Mr. Likic in order to round off this story about Vares Majdan and the trenches that were facing it. This is a photo that you already saw yesterday. I marked it by number 4. Can you please put it on the ELMO, and we will define certain things based on this photo. Yesterday in this photo, in its part that depicts your village and is facing Vares Majdan, you showed us bunkers on -- into parts in the left and in the right. Did I -- do my markings match your marks as you put them in the photo yesterday?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How shall I call this? The sentry point has to be moved a bit further down toward the so-called Botuk [phoen], and as for the X marking this is Stijencica, and this is correct. This is the entrance from Prnjavor.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Could you please take the pen and mark the exact positions and correct where I was wrong. Please mark the exact places where the trenches were, where the bunkers were.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Put a circle around that and number 1 next to that circle.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: And also mark the second bunker, the second trench, the place where they were.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's in the same place.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Can you please put a number 2 next to that.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: And at the right bottom side of the picture where you see Vares Majdan, can you please put a number 3 next to that.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you very much. This is Vares Majdan, isn't it? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Can you please put the full photo on the ELMO. Thank you. Okay. This is very similar. In the previous footage we saw two bunkers. One was made of wood, and the other one also contained sandbags or earth bags. It was well fortified, wasn't it? The thing that you marked by number 2, is that Borova Glava?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is Stijencica.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Stijencica?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Towards Pajtov Han, i.e., towards Prnjavor.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Very well, then. Yes. And where then would be Borova Glava according to you? Where is the Borova Glava a trench that you spoke about a little while ago, you mentioned it?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can't see it in this photo but you can -- it would be towards me but in a different photo.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Can you place an arrow pointing in the direction of Borova Glava, please? We will try and talk more slowly and try not to overlap, because the interpreters cannot follow. My question is this: Can you please put an arrow on the photo in the direction of Borova Glava?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Mr. Likic, I have here in front of me the trenches around the village of Stupni Do, so show P 09399. 9399.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, you've just shown trenches number 1, trench number 2, and number 3, which is the Vares village. In the middle of the photograph we can see your own village covered in snow.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. So the village is in the middle of the photograph. Here is my question: When the HVO troops attacked to take those two trenches, from which direction did they come? Did they arrive from Vares, number 3, or did they come crossing the village? Do you have any information on this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, and I can tell you. This trench, number 1, Potok, as it was called, the HVO soldiers arrived there by the road straight from Vares Majdan to the village of Stupni Do. Across, I mean. There's a road connecting the straight and one round about. Now, when the soldiers took Bogos hill, they went down the left-hand side and took the one where the arrow is, and then there's a hamlet lower down where they killed the people I said they'd killed yesterday, those ten people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Thank you. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: As we'll need this later on, would you please mark that place that you've just told us about, Prica Do, where as you say these ten people were killed. You can probably see that very well there, so where is that Do and where are those houses?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Thank you. Put a number 4 there then, please.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: And as I read in your statement, you went there at a certain point in time, and from there you went to your own house. So could you mark in your house now.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: And put a number 5 there, please.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Thank you. May we put the date on the photograph and have the witness's signature and then an IC number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please write your initials on the photograph, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Or your name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's have a number for that photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the photograph will become Exhibit IC 784. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Mr. Likic, can we agree on a military question now. According to what we've seen on this photograph and the other photographs, the bunkers that you marked on the other photographs previously, whether the trenches around the village were made in a circle. That is to say they encircled the village along the possible axes of attack. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the trenches around the village were in a circle surrounded with Potok, Stijencica, Bogos, Do, Borova Glava, Raskrsce, and Bradica.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Thank you. So we can agree that it was a circular defence for the village?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Now I'd like to go through exactly what you -- the way you moved because that wasn't done properly. The night before the attack onwards. So I'm going to ask you simple questions, and I hope to receive simple answers from you. The document, the P document that I had up is P 09399 and -- Witness, that's the documents that you made the markings on; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: And you've signed it, and you agree that that's how the trenches were situated?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And that's what the photograph shows.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we'll take it slowly. In the night between the 22nd and the 23rd of October, 1993, you stood guard at the locality that you indicated to us.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Borova Glava.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Borova Glava. Yes. Right. Now, on the 23rd, at 7.15, you were sitting in your house waiting for a cup of coffee when the attack started; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The attack began -- I didn't have a watch, but it began at around 8.00 or maybe five minutes past 8.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: All right. Now, at that time you took up your weapon and went towards Bogos hill, a place called Ravasnica, and you indicated that to us on an earlier photograph. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: We don't have to repeat that then. You then say in your statement, the statement you gave, that there were 11 soldiers there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Ten or 11 is what I said.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Right. And then you went on to say that the fighting lasted an hour and a half?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I said approximately. I didn't have a watch. Let me repeat again. I don't know exactly how long it went on for. I was speaking approximately because I didn't have a watch on my arm.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Well, two and a half hours or three hours, it's not important. Roughly, you say. Now, then after two and a half, three hours, your wife Kada came; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: After that, in your statement you say that after that time, and that is to be found on page 4 of the text that I have -- so with two women that makes the number of people up to 13. And then you say that some people left you at that time, and the people who were left was you, Vejsil, Nihad, Enver, and Suvaid, and two women, that they stayed in Ravnica; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: After that five of the 11 left, and you say they left to defend the village?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that two or three soldiers ran to the village.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Mr. Likic, I'm just counting. You say there were 11 plus two women. That makes it 13. Then you say you Vejsil, Nihad, Enver, and Suvaid stayed, and that makes it six men and two women. So five people. And then you go on to say: "And the rest went down to the village to defend their families." That's what it says in the statement?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true, but it needn't mean three because I wasn't -- I thought I could be killed any moment, so I wasn't fully aware of what was going on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: That's why we're speaking -- talking slowly here and taking it step-by-step. But anyway, in this statement you say that these five people went to the village to defend their families. Does that mean that they took their rifles with them, the rifles they had?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me explain. Your Honours, quite frankly and sincerely, we as soldiers in Stupni Do only had 28 barrels. However, there were 11 of us up there. So those 11 perhaps only had six weapons. Just six. You understand that? Maybe it was even five. And so if anyone were to be killed or wounded, then we went to take over the weapons and to continue shooting if there was any ammunition left. So that, friend, is what happened, how things were. And I state quite honestly that that's what it was, but we did not all of us, all 11 of us, have weapons.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Mr. Likic, I don't want to contradict you. I wasn't there at all. I'm just trying on the basis of the statement to reconstruct what happened together with all the other people here in the courtroom. So I'm just asking you a logical question. If five people, according to your statement, you say went to defend their families, would you not ask the same question? If they were going to defend their families then probably they have weapons with them. That's a simple question?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of those five there might have just been one or two weapons. And I repeat that. And they went down to the village. They rushed down to the village. It doesn't mean that they all had weapons. And we did not -- they did not all have weapons. I told you exactly and frankly how many weapons we actually did have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, we need a specific answer to this -- to that question. When your wife came to see you and to tell you that they were asking you to surrender, it means that the HVO was already in the village. So there were HVO fighters, armed men, in the village. Somebody comes and asks you to surrender. You're telling General Praljak then five men out of the 11 who were with you went to the village. Were they carrying weapons or not? That's the question. Because if they leave with a weapon, it means that there will be some shooting, because of course the other men in the village will see armed soldiers coming towards them and they might shoot at them. So are you telling us that they went to the village to defend -- they could defend even without having their weapons with them at that time? So can you remember? Did they have weapons when they left or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that they might have one or two rifles, but not all of them had rifles. They mostly went to see their families to see what had happened to them, those that hailed from the village itself. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Mr. Likic, all right. Please do not think that I'm trying to put words into your mouth. I am just asking questions based on which -- on what you stated. These people that ran into the village to defend it, according to you and had one or two or I don't know how many rifles, did they wear military uniforms, at least partly? Did some of them wear trousers or blouses or boots? Did they have parts of uniforms on them?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They looked very colourful. Some had normal clothes, some had trousers. They did not all have the whole uniform as the army would.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: In your statement you say that those of you who stayed went to Budozelj to inform the BH army to send help; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Further on you stated that later on four men had left you, Enver, Nermin, Suvaid, and Harad [phoen], and they went to Budozelj; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Three men left us, not four. Two stayed with me together with two women.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Very well. You said four, and I'm just asking. Now you're saying three.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The numbers don't have to match. It was really a lot of the psychosis in the air. That's why I'm not sure about the numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: I know, sir, how it looks. That's why we're going through things slowly taking things one at a time. Dzafer Rasim and Fadil Likic stayed with you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: And you and Kemal Likic [as interpreted] stayed on together with two women; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: After that you ran across a clearing. You were shot at, and as for the two women they were not shot at. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: On same day, at 19.45 on the 23rd of October, 1993, at 19.45 hours you arrived at Pecina?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was the so-called Stijene above Pajtov Han.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: At 21.30 hours or thereabouts you skirted Bogos; is that correct? And you arrived at Pajtov Han on the 24th of October, 1993, approximately around 2.00 after midnight; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Fadil Likic also left you at the time and went to Budozelj?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He left us on the following night, not on that night. You can read it in my statement that it was on the following night.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Dzafer Rasim stayed together with you and with the two women; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: And now let's talk about that night and about Monday the 25th October 1993 when you started walking towards the village to see what had happened. You were hungry. You were thirsty.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. Can you repeat the date?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: It was Monday.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Monday, the 25th of October.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Was it at around 8.00 in the morning?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's when we left Stijene and started walking towards our village.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Very well. And you arrived in your own village around 11.00 and 30 [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was not in the village but above the village.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: You arrived in Prica Do that we marked?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even further from Prica Do. Here, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: In Krcevine; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what is known as Krcevine.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Krcevine, Prica Do?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: And this is where you stayed to see what had happened in the village. You observed the situation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: And then you observed people coming into the village and this is something that is not of any interest to me. What I would like to hear from you is this: Did you see that on 25th of October, the day when you observed the village, an UNPROFOR vehicle entered the village carrying Mr. Martin and Ivica Rajic; did you notice that from the place where you were?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No I didn't.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Very well, then you did not notice anything on the 25th. And now towards the end of the day, we're talking about Monday, when it was already getting dark the had sun set as you said, you arrived at your house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was already dark when I arrived at my house.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Very well then. And now it says Rasim stayed outside and waited for me; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He stayed above my house.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: And you entered the house?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: And you say that you found something that looked like a body that was lying on -- on its stomach; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found three women's bodies.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Hold on. Hold on. You will find that later. First you found something that looked like a body, and I'm quoting your own statement. "I came upon something that looked like a body that was lying on its stomach. I saw that it was a charred and some pieces of meat were hanging from its flanks." Please. I went numb immediately and I thought that could be the body of my own son Adis." And you go on and say I decided to carry the body and bury it in the nearby Muslim cemetery. Now I would like to hear from you this: Did you find this body in the house?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found this body as I was approaching the house and the pavement above the house.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Very well then. And this was the body of Merima Likic?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: You say that the body was outside of the house on the pavement.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the -- next to the pavement if you know where the pavement is.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Yes I do. Thank you. And she was completely burned but you recognised the stockings and you could tell that it might have been Merima Likic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: And then you entered the house --

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I entered the cellar.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: The cellar. And you saw the bodies of Nevzeta and Hatidza and Medina in the pit that you used to store potatoes?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: You say here that you wanted to bury the body of Merima Likic in the nearby cemetery. Did you do that?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At first I thought when I saw the body -- actually, when the saw the women's stockings, before that I thought that this was the body of my son that was killed not far from there.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: But when you saw that this was a woman, you did not bury the body.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: The late Mrs. Medina is the same Medina who was a member of the BiH army. She was a soldier of the BH army, wasn't she?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question? I didn't understand it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: In the pit there were three bodies.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: The Medina whom you saw, was she wearing a camouflage uniform, and was she a member the BiH army?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Medina Likic only had a military vest on her body, nothing else. She had been a member of the BH army because she was the main cook who prepared lunches for the BiH army.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And let's finish with this. On the 25th, in the evening when you saw when you saw what you saw, you say that you went away from the place, that you left the place, and that in the morning on the 26th, and now we're talking about Tuesday, 26th of October, 1993, at 6.00 in the morning, UNPROFOR received you because they had been inviting people to approach them, and they took you to the free territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: In the first statement that you provided, to the OTP on the 16th of March -- I apologise. The statement was provided in 1996. In the second statement that you provided in 1998, I believe in 1998, actually, 1998, you now -- actually on the 28th of October, 1998, you now add -- added something to what you'd seen in your cellar, and you say that the three persons that you saw in your cellar had been massacred. Hatidza had her throat slit and her left breast had been cut off. "When I grabbed Nevezta's head to lift her head I could see that her left side of the face had been massacred, and chiseled. Medina looked like as if she had been sleeping. I did not notice any wounds of her -- on her body simply because I didn't want to touch her." My first question sir is this: How come did you not say all that in your first statement? How come you did not describe things as precisely as that? Why do your first statement and the second statement different in these very gruesome but very important details?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the first statement? What year was that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: In 1996 you only said that you saw three bodies. In your first statement in 1996 you say: "I descended into the cellar of my house that had been burnt completely."

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: "I lit a lighter and I saw Nevzeta, Hatidza and Medina's bodies in the pit we used to store potatoes. There was a big red candle lying beside the pit. There were wooden planks and some sacks inside the dead cellar. I pushed them aside thinking or hoping into my son might be hiding behind them, but it was a vein effort and you started looking for bread and so on and so forth. That's the first statement. The second statement is the statement that says this: "Hatidza's throat had been slit. She had been slaughtered. Her left bosom had been cut off. Nevzeta's left face had been smashed," and you also added that the red candle bore the markings of the HDZ and that it bored the word HDZ.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Sir, I understand these are terrible details, gruesome details one retains for their whole life, but I would like to know this: How come did you not provide all these details in the first statement? Why your description lacked all these details. How come that only your second statement contained all those details?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me put it this way and be very frank: In the first statement I said that there were three bodies; that's correct. That they had been massacred, but I did not provide any details as to how they had been massacred.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Praljak.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That they were killed. And in the second statement I provided details. I said that they had been massacred and that Hatidza's throat had been slit and her breast had been cut off. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the first statement I did not want to say all that because of the neighbours that lived next door. That was the only reason, the only reason. There was no other reason. I did not want to hurt their feelings. I did not want to upset them again. Those were my neighbours, my friends. Nevzeta was even my relative, my cousin's wife.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Very well then. Thank you. Now I would like to know this: In the second statement you say: "Three days later UNPROFOR found five more bodies in the part of the house that I had not visited, and they had all been charged -- they had all been charred, those bodies." Tell me, please, according to everything that we know here in this court UNPROFOR entered Stupni Do on the 26th of October, 1995. 1993 the soldiers entered together with the journalists, the investigators, and the civilian police of the United Nations entered Stupni Do, and they counted heads in the village, and they made a video footage. In that video footage one could see the three dead bodies that you mentioned, and we saw this video footage several times. I can run it again for you. And despite all my effort I did not see any signs of massacre on those bodies as you describe it. We're not going to see the footage again. Obviously we could. The footage depicts three bodies laying over each other. I don't know whether anybody had thrown a grenade or not, but what you're describing according with what I saw, I couldn't see any of that. Since there is a video footage of the whole thing, is it possible that at that moment you could not count the number of rifles that were taken to the village? Is it also possible that you could not see the bodies well? Medina was on top in -- wearing a uniform. How could you see the other bodies lying beneath her if you had left them in the same way you found them and in the same way that UNPROFOR found them when they entered the village? Is it possible that in your condition, carrying just a small cigarette lighter in your hands, could you maybe see the picture differently? Maybe you could see things that had not happened, actually. Is that possible? Is that a possibility?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I answer now?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Merima was lying to the right, to the right, like this. She seemed to be sleeping. I didn't want to disturb her. I lifted Nevzeta up by her hair and her body, her cheek was resting against the potatoes, and Hatidza, I just moved and put her back and there was blood here. That's what I did. With a lighter, you know, it's dark, you have a lighter. So that's what I was able to see, and that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Mr. Likic. Now, in your statement you -- to the Prosecutor, and you were up there, you said that you don't know whether from your basement there was any shooting.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, how could I know when I wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: So you can't testify about that. Perhaps one of those people -- Medina, perhaps, might have had a rifle and might have shot at someone through the window in your basement. You can't know that, can you?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that, but I said earlier on that we didn't have that many weapons for everybody to be -- to have a weapon to carry, because there were 42 fighters and just 28 barrels.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Well, the maths doesn't help us there, but you cannot know either way --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have the feeling that you've overstepped your time, so you need to conclude. There's a question which you should have been asked that hasn't been asked and which I shall put to you. Your house, was it a house that was fortified in the cellar or not? In other words, had you fortified in some manner the cellar of your house or hadn't you done anything about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't do anything. It's a basement that was made to keep your winter provisions in just with an entrance. And there's nothing else. There was the basement for the winter preserves, and the upper part where we lived with just with a partition wall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To your knowledge a young woman who was carry -- or wearing a camouflage uniform, who was cooking for the ABiH unit, could this person perhaps have held a gun in her hand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That person didn't have any weapon. Please believe me when I say that. I was there. I know how many weapons we had, and that particular person didn't have a rifle, a gun.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Two other women who were with her, could they have had a rifle or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you asking me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You told us that the woman who cooked was carrying no weapons. What about these two other women who were there? Could they have had a rifle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And why could they have a rifle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I wasn't there, so I don't know. I can't say. I can just assume that they didn't have any, because I know how many weapons we had.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Praljak, you will have to finish now. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'll be done very quickly.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: In your statement, in two places you mention dum bullets and say that you saw a member of the BH army who was killed with a -- and that he had a large hole in his back, and you said that that was cause the by the dum-dum bullets. And then in another place you say that you heard somebody shooting in a trench using dum-dum bullets. Could you explain to Their Honours what these dum-dum bullets are and what the difference is when you shoot with an ordinary bullet and when dum-dum bullets are used?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I made the statement as it stands. However, in my statement I said that I assume that Zejnil Mahmutovic, whom I found lying on his stomach face down, had a large bloody hole on the back, so I assume that he might have been killed by a dum-dum bullet because of this large hole in his back. Now, this other -- I heard these dum-dum bullets firing. Sort of -- there's a shot once and then another shot later on. I'm not a military expert to be able to explain this to you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. That's not how dum-dum bullets work. They enter the body and then explode and that's why they're dum-dum or expanding bullets. They weren't available.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I apologise then.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: When you waited to return to Stupni Do, you saw an HVO APC --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps, Your Honour, because of the overlapping a sentence was omitted when the witness said yes, and I apologise then when Praljak gave his opinion about the dum-dum bullets.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not a military expert, so I'm not well-versed in different types of ammunition. I thought that that was something else. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Let's just summarise what you say you saw the HVO had. They had an APC; right?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. While I was until the Stijene locality for two nights, I spent two nights there, you understand, the first night I wasn't able to pull out between the HVO trenches and go towards free territory with the women, so we went back. We returned and spent two days in the forest looking at what was going on around us. To the left you have Bogos hill and to the right you have Perun hill or, rather, the village of Planinica. Now, in between there's the Vares Majdan road going on to Breza and so forth, and the check-point was set up at the -- on the road to the Han where the village -- where the road to Strijezovo Selo goes. The APC which was made from a mining truck that I knew about because I earnt my pension working in a mine in Vares, in Treskavac [phoen], it was a mining truck that was covered in camouflage, and it went from Vares Majdan to Pajtov Han to that check-point and back several times. We saw it go there and back several times. Now, the other trucks --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. That's something you saw. Now let me ask you this: You also saw that an on a smaller truck --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You need to finish now, because the Bench is getting somewhat impatient. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may we just note that the HVO, according to the witness's statement, an anti-aircraft 20-millimetre machine gun.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Is that right?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Did you also see on a large truck a large-calibre Bofors anti-aircraft cannon?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not an expert. There was something like a machine-gun. There were different types of weapons anyway.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: That's what I wanted to tell Your Honours. We saw that there were 170 men at one point and 140 at another point and that with weapons like that you could blow-up the whole village because these weapons destroy all the walls and everything. So it's important to know what the HVO had so that we know how the operation evolved and whether there was any sense to it or not. Thank you, Mr. Likic. Thank you, Your Honours, for allowing me the time to ask the questions.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one question. I'm surprised as far as military logic is concerned. A military operation that aimed at taking control of Bogos and the village does not wish to target the trenches and take control of these trenches. This is why I would like to have your feeling about it even if you're not a high-ranking officer like General Praljak. In military terms, I don't understand thousand things happen sequentially. So if you leave soldiers in a trench, if you go and send out your wife to ask to surrender, supposing you were holding a mortar. You could have caused a tremendous amount of damage on the -- other side, the HVO troops. So why didn't they take control of all the trenches given that one vehicle was equipped with an anti-aircraft -- 20-millimetre anti-aircraft weapon? So how can you explain this to us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can explain that. These vehicles -- now, I didn't say whether they were the Bofors type as the man said, or an anti-aircraft cannon or whatever. There were two weapons on two trucks and Pajtov Han and Strijezevo were targeted and behind them there were groups of soldiers at Vares Majdan and Planinica. They didn't shoot at my village. It's a different hill, Perun hill, when I was at the Stijene locality that's what I saw where I spent two nights and went back on the third day, the Monday, up above the village. Now, I didn't understand the last part of what you said. I didn't understand your last question. Ah, yes, you asked about the mortar where I was. Where I was, the village of Radionica. When the women came to me there were no trenches. They had taken control of Bogos and we moved towards Bogos to help our guards there and that's where we met. There were no trenches there, no mortars there. And I heard that there was a 60-millimetre mortar in the village but I never saw it to be quite honest, Your Honours, and I didn't hear when it was used either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Alaburic to finish, even though my colleague has just told me that it is time to have the break. Ms. Alaburic, how many minutes do you need?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Your Honour, I think about 15 minutes if the witness can answer all my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, we shall have a 20-minute break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Alaburic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Witness, I would like to greet you and everybody in the courtroom. Mr. Likic, I would like to try and explain a detail that you may remember and that you may also not be aware of, and it concerns the basement in your house where the three women's bodies were found. In a document issued by UNPROFOR that we have already adopted in evidence in this case, and I'm talking about document under number D 6978, and I'm going to be referring to parts and the bullet point 3, a one in this document issued by UNPROFOR, it says that in the basement ten bullet cases of unknown calibre were found. It is also established that there were two small-sized windows covered by sandbags. And in conclusion it is stated that it is possible that this was a fortified facility from which fire had been opened. Tell me, please, did you notice bullet cases when you entered the basement?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I entered the basement there were no bullet cases. And as for the sandbags, there were no sandbags on the windows. I am saying again this is a small basement that was used for potatoes, and there were no windows. There are no windows to this day.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. Can you explain to the Trial Chamber how come that the list of soldiers that were killed in Stupni Do that were shown to you by my learned friend from the Prosecution says that the fighters were from Dabravine. Do you remember that document or do you want me to show it to you again to refresh your memory? This is document number P 8461 in the Prosecutor's binder of documents. This is a document that you saw and identified people who had the status of BiH soldiers.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You want me to explain?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Yes. Can you explain why Dabravine of all places?

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Just for the point of clarification, this is in fact entitled a list of residents killed in Stupni Do and not a list of fighters. It happens that the witness did identify a number of the ABiH members, BiH members in the list, but it's principally a list of residents, and I think it would be a misdescription entered in the record -- left in record described as a list of ABiH fighters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, the list is entitled "List of persons killed in Stupni Do in the municipality," and in that list there is a column with civilians and soldiers. Please proceed, Ms. Alaburic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is no doubt that this document also contains information about civilians, but what I'm interested in at the moment is information about soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In addition to the individuals whom you identified as BiH army soldiers, there's also the entry Dabravine soldier. Why Dabravine?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I can explain, of course, why Dabravine fighter. All the fighters that UNPROFOR located and found and that were taken to the free territory and could not be buried in the village of Stupni Do were buried in the village of Dabravine, and that's why it says a Dabravine fighter denoting where the burial place was. This doesn't mean that this person hailed from Dabravine.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you for this explanation. Tell me whether the command post of the Vares Brigade of the BiH army was in Dabravine?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In Dabravine was it where the War Presidency of Vares was also located?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, whether the commander of the BiH army unit in Dabravine was Mr. Ekrem Mahmutovic.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And the unit of the BiH army that was in Stupni Do, was it part of that 322nd Brigade from Dabravine?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so. I really wouldn't know. This is not something that I understand. I'm not an expert.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You told us that the commander of this military unit in Stupni Do was Mr. Himzo Likic and that he had been arrested some seven days prior to the attack against Stupni Do. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us who stood in for him as commander of the BH army unit in Stupni Do?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. It was Suvaid Likic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. As a member of the BH army, where did you receive your meals? Did you receive meals in your own house or did you go to a common place?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We all received our meals in our own houses save for the times when we were on the line. We received food that had been prepared elsewhere. Our trenches were far away from our homes. That's why food was brought to us.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Likic, did you ever hear, as we did, that an order reached Stupni Do from Dabravine on the 22nd of October, on the eve of the attack, ordering that the village should be evacuated because of the expected HVO attack? Did you ever hear a piece of information to that effect?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've never heard any such thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did you ever hear that on the eve of the attack in the village of Stupni Do the population held a meeting which was a meeting of the local commune or the village council and that the villagers decided as to what should be done, whether they should be mobilised, whether the Defence should be organised, or whether they would possibly be evacuated? Did you ever hear of that meeting?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never heard of that meeting either.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I would like to confront you with part of the testimony by Mr. Husnija Mahmutovic who testified in this courtroom and said something about the questions that I've just put to you. His statements are contained in document number P 10015. He told us that the villagers of Stupni Do had expected an HVO attack because the brother of one of your neighbour, who was a Croat, had arrived in the village and took out the entire family. Based on that Husnija Mahmutovic and other witnesses from Stupni Do had concluded that the HVO was preparing an attack on Stupni Do. Are you familiar with the fact that Mr. Husnija Mahmutovic mentioned?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I heard that only later on when the attack had already been finished.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mahmutovic went on to say that the village council was in session and decided to mobilise all the population of the village and to prepare them to defend the village. You are saying that you are not aware of that meeting or of that decision?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, and I'm telling you honestly that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mahmutovic went on to say that all the trenches that we have seen these days had been completely arranged and some few -- a few kilometres away from the village, that on the eve of the attack the villagers inspected all the trenches, checked that everything was in place, that they inspected the protection of the houses by sandbags, that they had established whether the supplies of water were sufficient to extinguish possible fires, that you had a short first-aid training, and that they were prepared in that way they expected that attack but that in principle they hoped that there would be no attack at all. Are you familiar with any of the circumstances that I've just mentioned to you?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I personally had a barrel of water by my house in case my house caught fire, to be able to extinguish that fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Likic, do you know that the BH army unit in Stupni Do had a radio set that they could use to communicate with the command post in Dabravine?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I never saw any such thing. I was just an ordinary soldier. I repeat, I just keep guard and then I would come home.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well, then. You have spoken, if I understood you well, about some members of the BH army who during the course of the attack abandoned their positions in the trenches and they started moving towards the centre of the village in order to either help their families or to defend them. Is that correct? Do I understand your testimony correctly?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no trenches where I was save for the two trenches that I marked next to the village, and only those people descended. They had one or two rifles. They ran through the village in order to see where their families were. At that moment the village did -- was not set ablaze. The fire started from my house towards the south.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. Is it true that there was an abandoned Serb house in the village as well?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There -- there were ten Serb houses in the village. They had left the village sometime in May. I can't remember the exact date. And they went to the Serb territory. However, two Serbs remained in the village of Puinsa [phoen] and Bebanrosovic [phoen] and they remained living with us. Their wives were Croats. One was from Mir and the other from Vares.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: For the time being I'm only interested in the Serb houses. And with regard to the house that you defined as your own and marked by number 5, where were the Serb houses that you've just mentioned? I believe that you still have on the ELMO the photo that you can use.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have it on the screen. I have it next to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now you have it on the screen as well. Can you please tell us and show us the picture's on e-court. Can you please tell us where those Serb houses were?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Please do then.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the usher please -- can the usher please help the witness to show these houses on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't see a Serb house here.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can't see a house here that was on the shortcut from Vares to Majdan, and there was a Serb house here. And this is the second house.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The third house is here behind my own house. And in the centre of the village there were two houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: This is enough.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And here above there are two more Serb houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Yes. We've had enough of the Serb houses. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And here two Serb houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If the Honourable Judges believe that it would be of some use to have the document with the locations of the Serb houses, I don't have anything against marking these locations and giving a new number to this photo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Alaburic, I don't see the point in saying that there are three Serb houses. What are you trying to show? I don't really understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I am trying to show this: First I'm trying to show that there were Serb houses in order to lay the foundation for my question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In an UNPROFOR document that we have seen in this courtroom, the village of Stupni Do was recorded as saying -- the document number is P 9121, bullet point 27(x) and (c). This gentleman said that at the beginning of the conflict two -- nine BH army soldiers were billeted in an abandoned Serb house in the village. Are you familiar with that? Do you know that some army members were billeted in an abandoned Serb house in the village on the eve of the attack?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with that at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: That same person went on to say that when the HVO had arrived within the site the BH army had withdrawn towards the centre of the village. My question is this: Are you familiar that some soldiers did withdraw towards the centre of the village regardless of where they had been before?
