utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with that. I don't know any such thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well then. Somebody also said that the shelter for the civilians in the centre of the village -- or, rather, that there was a shelter for civilians in the centre of the village which was defended by 14 member of the BH army. Now, are you familiar with that fact?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I can tell you is what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Well, go ahead and tell us what you heard.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I show this? It's this house here at the outskirts of the village where all the people rallied together. They came from the village and met here when the shooting started here from my house towards this area here, and that's where the house was defended, because there were about 200 people there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now would you place an X, an X on that house, please, the one you said was the main shelter for the civilians and that everybody gathered there. And then --

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I'd like an IC number for the photograph with these new markings, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The map already has an IC number. The witness in red has just marked the house where civilians had rallied. The transcript will help us understand the indications given by the witness unless we can give another IC number. Can we give another IC number to that exhibit or -- no. It is not possible. So we'll keep the same IC number, but we'll just remember that at a later stage the witness marked the house where these people had rallied together with the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to thank Judge Antonetti for that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Likic, in this courtroom we heard that it was from this position near the shelter that Amir Likic threw a grenade on HVO soldiers. Did you hear about that?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He threw a hand grenade [as interpreted], not a grenade, to save the people who were in his house.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now, up until that time, up until the time that this bomb was thrown or hand grenade, the HVO did not attack in any way that particular house in which so many civilians were located; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't give you an answer because I wasn't there and everything that I've told you is based on what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, in a document the following was also recorded and it is document P 6978, point 38(c) where it was stated that the defence forces of the BH army were concentrated around the main village shelter where most of the civilians were located. And you've just told us that indeed the BH army soldiers did turn up in the vicinity and that a bomb was thrown. Now, the question is is it true that the defence forces were concentrated around that particular shelter?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What defence forces?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Members of the BH army. That those members of the BH army who did not leave the village, who did not go to Budozelj were concentrated around the shelter in which the civilians were located?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I heard, but let me repeat, I wasn't there myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right, fine. Now, according to the information we've had so far, the HVO attack lasted roughly for about six to seven hours, and during that time the HVO did not succeed in taking control of the whole village. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me repeat again and I apologise, but I did not see it myself. I wasn't there. I was up in the forest and went with the women to the other side of Bogos.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, Mr. Likic, as you did not hear anything else. I have no further questions for you, and I'd like to thank you.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Flynn, would you like to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Just two or three questions. I hope they will be short, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Likic. You were asked --

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: You were asked during the course of the day -- certain questions were put to you regarding Ms. Medina Likic that described -- you said her status was a fighter although you described her as a cook for the ABiH and she was cooking for the forces. When you say her status was a fighter, did you ever see her take up a weapon? Do you know did she possess a weapon?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I object to this question because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You must leave Mr. Flynn ask the question. Ms. Alaburic. Ms. Alaburic, I have made a decision. You cannot challenge my decision, so please let Mr. Flynn ask the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I ask it be record rod --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Alaburic, Article 46, if you continue so. Please sit down and Mr. Flynn will ask his question, we'll hear the answer of the witness, and if need be you'll be allowed to ask your question. But for the time being let Mr. Flynn ask his question. You are taking the floor on a particular question which I've already put to the witness and the witness has already provided answer. So, Mr. Flynn, what is your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: My question once again is in answer to Mr. Kovacic this morning -- or this afternoon you said that her status was a fighter, and you described her later as a cook working for the ABiH. Did you ever see her engaged in fighting? Do you know did she possess a weapon?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never saw her fighting. She never possessed a weapon. All she had was a military vest on her. She just cooked for the forces, so that's why she had this status of fighter or combatant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Alaburic, what's the problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, all I wanted to say is this: The status of the member of the army is not determined by the fact that somebody cooks, is a cook, or whether is he is the commander of a military unit, and that is why this question, if one wants to clarify what she actually did, is subject to that. So my objection would be in conformity the Geneva Conventions and how members of the armed forces of one party in a conflict are defined.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, was this lady a member of the ABiH or was she just a civilian cooking? Could you please answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, she was a member of the army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. But I'm not a military analyst, and as I heard it, she was proclaimed a fighter, and she was killed, but what she did was cook lunches and dinners for the soldiers of the BH army in the village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Flynn.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Just following up on that. You told us that food was brought to the BiH members when they were out on the line. Did you ever see Ms. Likic bring food to the soldiers in the trenches?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Thank you. Turning -- turning to the video that was shown to you earlier where a number of trenches were depicted in the video, you weren't able to recognise some of those. I just wanted to ask you if you know during the period that the HVO occupied Stupni Do, do you know if during that period they themselves built any kind of fortifications or trenches?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat that question, please? I'm not sure I understood it properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: You will remember the video that was shown to you showing a number of trenches, one of them overlooking Vares Majdan?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And there were a number of other trenches. You were not able to recognise some of those trenches. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: I'm wondering if you can tell us during the period that the HVO occupied Stupni Do, which we believe from the evidence given before this panel, was certainly for a period of three to four days after the attack, do you know from your own knowledge or from what you've heard if the HVO constructed fortifications and trenches themselves?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if you allow me before the witness answers. There is a suggestion in the answer. Did the HVO build any trenches. That cannot be a question. The question can be whether anybody after HVO took position build the trenches. That perhaps maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: If you wish to put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Do you know if anybody else built trenches during the period that HVO were in occupation of the village?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. When the HVO held the village, you weren't allowed to enter. You couldn't enter, and I didn't hear about it either, to be quite honest.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And when you returned to the village, did you see signs -- did you see signs of any new trenches having been dug?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no new trenches had been dug.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And lastly, from any of the trenches which the ABiH had surrounding the villages, and in particular those trenches facing Vares Majdan, do you know whether or not there was any firing on the town of Vares Majdan from those ABiH trenches at any stage prior to Stupni Do?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL LIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me explain, Your Honours. Not a single trench was turned towards Vares Majdan or anything. This trench at Borova Glava was facing -- I said in the first version towards Vares Majdan. However, I do apologise. It was turned towards the Nesiska [phoen] Plateau and the Serb village and towards the village of Mir, while the other trench on Stijencica from which you can see Vares Majdan as well, if you understand me, was facing Prnjavor, not towards Vares Majdan. Now, the only thing is that the trench in Potok, the first trench in Potok, and next to it was a small house, that faced the road leading to Vares Majdan, straight to Vares Majdan, but from there you couldn't see the town and the forest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is an extremely simple problem. Before the HVO attacked your village, I do say before, did a soldier of the ABiH ever fire at Vares Majdan? Could that have happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, never. They never shot in the direction of Vares Majdan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're positive about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm quite sure of that. At least according to what I saw. Now, what I didn't see I can't be sure of.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I don't have any further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So on behalf of my colleagues, I would like to thank you for having come to testify and help us understand the events that unfolded in your country. I wish you a safe journey home. I shall ask the usher to escort you now out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Trial Chamber will first of all move into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I shall read slowly the decision, and I will check the English translation. Oral decision on the application presented by the Petkovic Defence presented yesterday by Mr. Stewart. At the hearing held on January the 16th, 2008, the Petkovic Defence counsel, through Mr. Stewart, asked the Chamber to be allowed to present its submissions on the modalities of implementation of Rule 98 bis before the beginning of the presentation of oral submissions pursuant to Rule 98 bis due to start on January the 28th, 2008. The Chamber reminds the parties of the Three Scheduling Orders issued on September the 27th, October the 22nd, and November the 22nd, 2007. The Chamber then granted each accused three hours to present these oral submissions pursuant to Rule 98 bis unless the accused decide among themselves, between themselves, to redistribute the time allotted to them in a different fashion. The Chamber also decided that the Prosecution's response should not exceed nine hours. Moreover, the Chamber ruled that there would be no reply to the Prosecutor's response and that written submissions would not be allowed. As a preliminary remark, the Chamber notes that the wording of Rule 98 bis, as well as the case law relating to that law, are unequivocal. Nevertheless, the Chamber is prepared to hear the parties on their interpretation of the Rule during their oral submissions due to start on January the 28th, 2008, and within their allotted time. Thus the Chamber dismisses the Petkovic Defence application for parties to be heard before the above-mentioned date. This was the Chamber's oral decision. To sum up, parties, as they wish to do so, will be free to present their submissions, but only from January the 28th during the three hours allocated to each Defence team. This was our oral decision as issued by this Chamber today. I also would like to indicate to all parties that several decisions were issued today and filed today, which means that there is very little pending at this stage. However, all decisions will be issued before January the 28th. This is all I wanted to indicate to the parties. If there's no other issue pending, we are going to adjourn the hearing, and we will invite you all to be here on Tuesday. The hearing will start at 9.00 a.m. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
